bullets.title: Iran/Hormuz tensions spike WTI +4.5% to $92+, driving broad risk-off
bullets.body: WTI crude surged ~4.5% to $92.19–$92.63 and Brent to $104.42 on Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, Iran strike concerns, and Strait of Hormuz tanker transit disruption (2-month lows). VLCC rates spiked to $1.4M/day on ME-Asia routes (6x pre-war). S&P futures fell 0.4–0.5% overnight, 10-year yield up 4–7 bps to 5.32–5.35%, and Nasdaq futures dropped ~80 bps as oil became the dominant tape driver.

bullets.title: 10-year yield at 5.32–5.35% (highest since 2007); macro tightening at 95th percentile
bullets.body: Treasury yields continued their rise with the 10-year touching 5.32–5.35% and the 2-year at 4.81%, the highest levels since 2007 per JPM's macro conditions indicator now above the 95th percentile (last seen during 2025 tariff escalation). The 10-year auction itself was strong with record-high indirect demand and record-low dealer participation, suggesting structural demand even at elevated yields. Fed Gov. Waller signaled further hikes likely but with timing flexibility; Fed minutes showed Oct hike probability fell from ~20% to ~17%, Dec from ~84% to ~78%.

bullets.title: Diesel +67% since Iran war; 15–20bp core inflation hit, but fading tariffs offset
bullets.body: Diesel has surged 67% since end of February (gasoline +46%), with the crack spread above 2022 highs, feeding into core inflation through shipping costs on domestic goods. Wolfe estimates a 15–20bp core inflation impact over the next year from freight cost increases, expected to be more than offset by fading tariff pass-through of 50bp+. Trucking and rail carry ~90% of domestically shipped goods, both running on diesel with highly inelastic demand.

bullets.title: Nasdaq/Russell positioning gap at 96th percentile — historically bullish for small caps
bullets.body: JPM flags the Nasdaq-vs-Russell positioning gap at +2.6 standard deviations (96th percentile), highest since Jan 2022. NDX net positioning sits at the 98th percentile long while Russell is at the 3rd percentile short (longs lowest in a year). In 6 of 9 prior instances when the gap hit the top decile, Russell outperformed Nasdaq over the subsequent period. Cyclicals vs. Defensives are down 2%+ this week; NDX has outperformed R2K on 17 of the last 20 sessions.

bullets.title: AI capex arms race: Broadcom, SpaceX, Oracle arranging $50B+ debt deals for chip purchases
bullets.body: Broadcom is arranging $50B+ financing for OpenAI's custom chip buildout and already launched $60B debt financing for Anthropic; SpaceX is pursuing $40B financing via Apollo to purchase Nvidia chips; Oracle is in talks with Apollo and Goldman for similar financing. This structural shift reflects frontier labs lacking balance sheet capacity and signals a multi-year supercycle in AI infrastructure demand with private credit playing a central role alongside traditional debt markets.

bullets.title: TSMC Q3 revenue +51–55% YoY to record $46.7B; Samsung memory profits beat on HBM
bullets.body: TSMC's Q3 revenue hit a record NT$1.49tn (~$46.7B), up ~51% YoY, beating consensus of NT$1.46tn entirely on AI demand. Samsung posted Q3 operating profit of W107.4tn, slightly below street but marking the fourth consecutive record quarter, with memory profits beating on DRAM/NAND margins and HBM growth. Samsung is qualifying 12-high HBM4E chips with Nvidia and hyperscalers; AMD CEO Lisa Su called for memory manufacturers to ramp HBM capacity, with HBM pricing expected to jump 100–150% next year.

bullets.title: Big Five hyperscale capex revised to +93% YoY in 2026; 2027 now seen >40% YoY
bullets.body: Citi raised its Big Five aggregate cloud capex growth estimate to +93% YoY for 2026 (up 10% from June), with 2027 growth revised higher to >40% YoY from >30% prior. Global data center supply is forecast to grow at a 23% CAGR from 140GW (2026) to 395GW by 2031, with a potential 'Power Wall' constraint emerging by 2028. Clean room space constraints in semi-cap equipment are expected to create pent-up demand through CY28/29.

bullets.title: Semi-cap equipment WFE estimates raised: $200B CY27, $260B CY28; AMAT top pick
bullets.body: Wolfe raised WFE estimates to $155B (CY26), $200B (CY27), and $260–280B (CY28), with clean room constraints limiting near-term upside but ensuring demand persists into CY29. AMAT is the top pick — up 102% YTD and best-performing SCE stock this year — with 40%+ operating margin guidance expected at Semicon West and valuation most attractive at ~20x CY28 bull-case P/E. ASML multiple compression from China underperformance viewed as transitory; positioned for price increases and >110 EUV tools in CY28.

bullets.title: Software Q3 setup: JPM favors MSFT/NOW/NET/SNOW on AI tailwinds; IGV +21% since June
bullets.body: JPM and Goldman both flag Infrastructure software leading on AI-driven estimate revisions while Application software benefits from multiple re-rating as fundamentals prove more resilient than feared. IGV is up 21% since end of June. Key Q3 expectations: MSFT ~10M+ Copilot seat adds with modest M365 monetization; NOW cRPO beat ~200bps with AI ACV target raise beyond $1.5B; SNOW accelerated migration pace; NET revenue acceleration to high-30% YoY from Workers/AI demand. HUBS downgraded at JPM on delayed AI monetization.

bullets.title: Goldman upgrades PLTR to Buy ($230 PT) on sovereign AI TAM step-function change
bullets.body: Goldman upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral with a $230 PT (18% upside), citing a moat that compounds via AI-augmented FDE feedback loops and U.S. government deployment expansion driving a TAM step-function change into 2027. PLTR trades at a discount (1.2x EV/FCF) to high-growth peers at 3x and has lagged SNOW/NET/DDOG (up 50–100% YTD vs. PLTR +9% YTD). Goldman simultaneously downgraded TYL to Neutral ($345 PT from $395) as the cloud adoption thesis is largely played out with no clear AI catalyst.

bullets.title: Q3 cybersecurity channel checks strongest since COVID; CRWD, OKTA, PANW all above plan
bullets.body: Roth's Q3 channel checks show cybersecurity closed 112% above plan vs. 108% a year ago — one of the best quarters since COVID. CRWD is at 10% above plan (Exposure Management and AIDR strength); PANW at 10% above plan (Cortex Cloud, Prisma, XSIAM with less discounting Aug–Sep vs. July); OKTA at 5–9% above plan; ZS ticked up to 5–9% above plan. Federal fiscal year-end spending was a healthy tailwind. Only CHKP ticked down (below plan 2–5%) on fading Harmony/Avanan products.

bullets.title: Geopolitical conflict transmission shifting to financial conditions: MOVE index near April 2025 dysfunction
bullets.body: Jefferies geopolitical analysis warns the Iran-US conflict is increasingly transmitted through inflation, Treasury yields, bond volatility, and financial conditions rather than physical crude scarcity. The MOVE index is rising sharply toward April 2025 dysfunction levels. Washington and Tehran are negotiating via Qatar but disagree on sequencing and verification; Yemen is emerging as an independent instability source requiring its own process. Military sustainability is increasingly constrained by interceptor inventories and competing strategic commitments.

bullets.title: Consumer spending (Chase data) accelerating: +6.6% YoY through Sept 29, up from 5.3% in August
bullets.body: JPM Chase card data shows consumer spending accelerating to +6.6% YoY through September 29 vs. +5.3% in August, with upper income +7.8%, middle +8.2%, and Gen Z/Millennials +9.4% YoY. Costco U.S. September comps confirmed the trend at +8.0% ex-gas with traffic +4.3% YoY — strongest since July FY25. Q3 ad spend grew 8.6% YoY, ~90bps above expectations, with ad buyers preserving dry powder for year-end despite rate concerns.

bullets.title: Equity capital markets surge: Global ECM $856B YTD (+60% YoY); IPOs strongest since 2021
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs reports global ECM issuance YTD at $856B (+60% YoY), the highest excluding 2021, with Americas at $514B (+90% YoY). Global IPO issuance hit $280B (+174% YoY) across 499 offerings — the strongest since 2021 — with Americas IPOs at $200B (+264% YoY). Notably, north of 50% of primary issuance ($481B, +118% YoY) is funding AI capex. Convertible issuance of $200B (+65% YoY) is on pace for a record year.

bullets.title: US midterm outlook: divided government constructive for healthcare/nuclear; data center permitting headwind
bullets.body: With Democrats favored to win the House (26-seat historical deficit for the president's party) but the Senate path narrower, a divided government would retain Trump admin authority over tariffs, deregulation, and foreign policy. AI regulation expected to remain benign — bipartisan focus on oversight/safety, not model constraints. Data centers face greater scrutiny on power, water, land use, and permitting under Democratic control (costs rise but construction not materially slowed). Healthcare services and managed care benefit from greater Democratic Medicaid leverage.

bullets.title: Bank earnings kick off Oct 13 (C, GS, JPM, WFC); macro deterioration a headwind
bullets.body: Bank Q3 earnings commence October 13 with C, GS, JPM, and WFC reporting. JPM flags macro deterioration — higher rates, higher oil, slowing demand — pressuring loan growth, fee generation, and credit performance. KEY's NIM guide reset to 3.00–3.05% vs. prior 3.25%+ target; NPLs rose sharply while reserves-to-loans fell to 1.56%. Jefferies' top bank picks into earnings are WFC, C, USB, EWBC, and WTFC. Treasury yields at 5.32% on the 10-year are adding headwinds across the sector.

bullets.title: Memory/Semis under pressure; rotation expected toward custom silicon (AVGO/MRVL) and semcap
bullets.body: Despite Samsung's record quarterly profit and TSMC's record revenue, investors are questioning whether record memory profits are priced in and whether margins are sustainable. Multiple sources flag likely profit rotation from memory into custom silicon (AVGO/MRVL) and semi-cap equipment. Micron and Nvidia alone are projected to drive ~one-third of S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth. Citi downgrades NXPI to Neutral (limited data center exposure) and OLED to Sell (smartphone weakness), while keeping AMD and TXN as top picks.

bullets.title: Asian equities in macro distress: KOSPI -27% from June peak; China, India weakening
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro framework flags South Korea KOSPI down 27.3% since June (Quad 4 crash), China Shanghai Composite down 3.3% in the last month, India equities down 6.2% in the last month (entering stagflation), and Germany/Switzerland equities down 4.3%/2.4% respectively. 72% of S&P stocks fell an average of 1.4% yesterday. The Russell 2000 is down 9% from its cycle peak. JPM flags KOSPI and Korean memory stock direction as essential to assessing any AI trade recovery in Japanese equities.

bullets.title: Connectivity and HDD storage emerge as Citi's highest-conviction AI infrastructure calls
bullets.body: Citi's coverage is up +125% YTD vs. S&P 500 +14%, led by storage, hardware OEMs, and connectivity. Citi is most bullish on connectivity components (APH, GLW) on a multi-end-market thesis that broadens beyond IT Datacom to Defense as a secular growth driver. HDD is preferred over NAND given lower competitive intensity and margin expansion potential; Toshiba's HDD expansion news is seen as creating attractive entry points for STX and WDC. Enterprise OEMs (DELL, HPE, AAPL) benefit from infrastructure modernization with supply chain management as a competitive moat.

bullets.title: Q3 internet ad spend +8.6% YoY, ~90bps above expectations; META and GOOGL best setups
bullets.body: Piper's channel checks show Q3 internet ad spend grew 8.6% YoY, approximately 90bps above expectations, with buyers preserving dry powder into year-end due to rising rate concerns. Strong verticals include AI, GLP-1s, sports, travel, tech, and movies; weaker in autos, CPG, and financials. META is up 18% since the Muse agentic launch and is seen by Piper alongside GOOGL as the best internet setup into earnings, while SNAP, PINS, and RDDT remain more mixed.
